title: unify-stream-backpressure-iterable-protocols-and-reauth-parity-across-sdks
author: Asha Patel
commits: 6 commits: initial-typescript-iterable-adapter; add-go-stream-iterator-and-reconnect; python-async-iterator-fallback; unify-auth-retry-abstractions; add-integration-tests-for-backpressure; bump-sdk-versions-and-changelog
description:
Context: There have been multiple customer reports and internal discrepancies around streaming ergonomics and how SDKs behave under backpressure + token rotation. The TS/Go/Python SDKs had subtly different streaming iterator contracts (pull vs push semantics), and reauth/retry hooks were implemented ad-hoc in each language. This PR unifies the iterable protocol across SDKs so applications can rely on consistent backpressure behavior, standardizes an auth-retry abstraction used by streaming helpers, and provides ergonomic adapters (async iterator for Python, IterableIterator for TS, a small iterator type for Go). Motivation: improve parity for cross-platform reference apps, reduce bug surface when routing streaming requests through gateways, and enable a single set of integration tests that catch regressions.

What this change does (high level): - Introduces a lightweight stream iterator shim in each SDK that exposes the same semantic guarantees: consumers can await/iterate until completion, early cancellation signals KV cache/connection cleanup, and backpressure instructs the runtime to pause prefetching. - Moves retry + token-refresh responsibilities into a shared auth/retry abstraction (language-specific thin wrappers) so streaming code does not duplicate handshake logic. - Adds reconnect + resume semantics for transient network errors: SDKs attempt short exponential backoff (configurable), then signal a resumable error to the consumer if available. - Adds integration tests for backpressure and reauth scenarios (TS and Python). - Bumps TypeScript SDK minor version, updates CHANGELOG and examples.

Checklist: - [x] TypeScript iterator adapter and docs - [x] Python async adapter and tests - [x] Go iterator + small examples - [x] Shared retry/auth abstraction implemented - [x] Integration tests for backpressure and token refresh - [x] CI green, version bump, changelog entry

Commits summary: initial Typescript iterable adapter and typing; adapt existing streaming client to use iterable API; add Python async adapter that decorates generator-based streams; implement Go iterator with context-aware cancellation; factor out auth retry behavior into sdk/common; add tests that assert pause/resume and token-refresh during streaming; bump TS SDK version to 4.3.0-rc1.
review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Nice consolidation. Two requests: (1) can we make the backpressure knob configurable per-stream with a sane default? (2) add a short example in docs showing early cancellation behavior (how connections are closed).
Asha Patel: Addressed both - added per-stream options (prefetch=1 by default) and a docs example that demonstrates early cancel cleanup (examples/streaming/* and docs/sdk/streaming.md).

Priya Rao: Found a race where python async adapter could call cleanup twice during cancellation+reauth; suggested moving cleanup into a single atomic path. Also asked for an extra unit test for double-cancel.

Asha Patel: Fixed by centralizing cleanup in the adapter base class and added unit test tests/unit/test_double_cancel.py. Pushed patch that consolidates cleanup and adds comment explaining ordering guarantees.

Daniel Kim: Go iterator looks good. Please add a small note in CHANGELOG that the SDK now exposes ResumeableStreamError for callers that want to implement custom retry logic. Approved after changelog tweak.
Asha Patel: Updated CHANGELOG and bumped TS package.json. Thanks!
ci_checks: unit:linux (first run) — failed (flake in python test_double_cancel)
release_notes: SDKs: unified streaming iterator protocol across TypeScript/Python/Go; added per-stream backpressure controls; standardized auth-retry hooks for streaming; added reconnect/resume semantics; TS SDK bump to 4.3.0-rc1. See docs/sdk/streaming.md for migration notes.
